certifications.name: GDPR Compliance

A Google Cloud case study identifies 'Michał Leszek, Director of Information Technology and Data Protection Officer at Brainly.' privacy.ai_training_note: Brainly builds its AI Learning Companion on its corpus of user-generated questions and answers. A Forbes profile (third-party, not a vendor-domain statement) describes Brainly 'leveraging its trove of authentic user data' and a 'massive trove of authentic student data' to develop the product. Brainly does not publicly document an opt-out mechanism or explicit AI-training consent. This is a data governance concern for a K-12 platform, though the training corpus is largely the platform's public Q&A community content rather than private tutoring data.
privacy.data_region: Global distribution (North America, Europe, Asia, Latin America via Google Cloud). Data NOT limited to EU regions despite GDPR compliance claims.
sources: https://brainly.com/pages/privacy_policy (stated: 'personal data might be transferred anywhere we or our partners operate')

flags: Brainly lacks SOC 2, ISO 27001, or other third-party security certifications typical of enterprise EdTech platforms. This is unusual for a company serving millions of K-12 students globally.

Brainly leverages student-generated content for AI training without clear evidence of an opt-out mechanism or explicit student/parent consent. This is a significant concern for a K-12 platform and a potential COPPA/GDPR violation risk.
Despite serving 15+ million users across 35+ countries, no public trust center or detailed security/compliance documentation is available.

An independent Common Sense Media review indicated the platform 'does not have a privacy policy and/or does not use encryption' (though a privacy policy exists; that review may be outdated). Its privacy and security ratings fall below standards for K-12 platforms.
Brainly claims GDPR compliance, but per its privacy policy data 'might be transferred anywhere' globally. Data storage is not EU-exclusive despite European operations and serving EU students.
The privacy policy and terms pages return 403 Forbidden errors when accessed directly, preventing independent verification of the terms.
Brainly handles subscription payments, but no PCI DSS certification or payment security details are published.
No public Data Processing Agreement template is available despite Brainly serving EU customers under GDPR; DPA availability is not confirmed.
Brainly serves users under 13 but lacks formal COPPA Safe Harbor certification, relying on a parental consent model with unclear enforcement mechanisms.
